channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: FAA ground stop live updates: Duffy blames 'overloaded' routers after stop lifted
item.description: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin said it was due to a "telecommunications outage."

item.title: Trump to meet with Putin and Xi in China next week, US officials say
item.description: Trump will participate in the first-ever trilateral meeting between the leaders of the U.S., China, and Russia on the sidelines of the APEC Summit in China next week.

item.title: 'Miracle': All rescued from capsized New Orleans riverboat in tanker collision
item.description: The incident occurred Friday on the Mississippi River.

item.title: Authorities say DC gunman held long-standing feud with building management
item.description: The 55-year-old medical doctor harbored a long-standing grievance with the building's condo association, according to court documents.

item.title: Sarah Huckabee Sanders receives 2028 presidential encouragement
item.description: Supporters and donors have been encouraging GOP Arkansas Gov. Sarah Huckabee Sanders to run for president in the 2028 cycle, sources told ABC News.

item.title: GOP state officials push to revive Trump's mail voting restrictions for 2028 election
item.description: Some Republican state officials are reviving a bid for mail-in voting restrictions for the 2028 election by appealing a court order blocking the Postal Service from carrying out a revised ballot rule.

item.title: FAA lifts the nationwide ground stop for all U.S. airports
item.description: The nationwide ground stop that paralyzed the U.S. aviation system on Friday has ended, according to Federal Aviation Administration.

item.title: Gambia's Adama Barrow seeks third term
item.description: In tonight's programme, Gambia's electoral commission has announced the five official candidates for the country's upcoming presidential election. President Adama Barrow is seeking a third term. Tensions continue to rise in Ethiopia following the federal government's appointment of a new head of the Western Tigray region. And the Dakar Youth Olympic Games come to a close after two weeks of intense competition.

item.title: France among five major powers to represent EU in Ukraine talks
item.description: European Council President Antonio Costa on Friday said that Brussels will send diplomats from the bloc and five countries, including the UK, France, Germany, Italy and Poland, to upcoming Ukraine talks.

item.title: US flight authority orders national ground stop over air traffic control 'communication issue'
item.description: The US flight authority on Friday halted flights across the nation due to what US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said was a communication issue affecting the country's air traffic control centres.

item.title: The government says it will close a beloved D.C. park Sunday. Will a judge step in?
item.description: Federal judge Ana Reyes grilled the government on Friday about its plans for East Potomac Park, and indicated she could order it to remain open despite President Trump's renovation wishes.

item.title: 'Miracle on the Mississippi': 180 rescued after cruise ship collides with tanker
item.description: More than 30 people have been taken to hospital after a tanker lost control and crashed into a cruise ship on the Mississippi River.

item.title: Turkey and Qatar pledge unified stance against attacks in mutual defence pact
item.description: Turkey and Qatar signed a mutual defence agreement Friday, pledging a unified response to any attack on either country, the two leaders said in a joint statement. The defence pact follows the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement signed by Turkey, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia in August.

item.title: The Downfall of AI’s ‘Rock Star’ Boss, Ukraine: Who speaks for Europe? Protests & Presidents
item.description: On The World This Week with Gavin Lee, our panel distills the breaking news and global stories of the past 7 days into 45 minutes. Ukraine: Who will speak for Europe? In a week thats seen the first direct talks between Ukraine and Russia since February, with the US in the room and the Europeans relegated to the lobby according to Moscow. A new ‘European Security Architecture’ is discussed.

item.title: Hurry up and wait: Europe wants a place at the table, ‘must make up its mind’ over Ukraine
item.description: Gavin Lee is pleased to welcome Alexander Titov, Lecturer in Modern European History at Queen's University Belfast and a specialist on Russia. He's joined us to discuss high-level meetings in Abu Dhabi, Dublin and the prospects for ending the war in Ukraine.

item.title: Schumer and Van Hollen face off for Senate majority leader. What do Democrats think?
item.description: Within moments of Chris Van Hollen announcing his intent to challenge Chuck Schumer in a race to lead next year’s Senate Democratic majority, endorsements began flying.

item.title: What's Trump's strategy now with Iran? To keep things as they are
item.description: President Trump says the "status quo" is what Gulf Arab allies want as the Iran war hits a stalemate and the U.S. midterms force a pivot from threats of attacks to economic pressure.

item.title: Probation staff vote for strike action in 'serious anger' over pay and workloads
item.description: Probation and family courts staff have voted in favour of strike action over pay and workloads.

item.title: What we know about China's military exercises around Taiwan
item.description: China has been carrying out major military drills around Taiwan since early November. But contrary to some claims on social media, Beijing's armed forces have not actually implemented a blockade on the island; they just simulated it.

item.title: Iran live updates: Bessent blasts Iranian threats
item.description: President Donald Trump announced "major combat operations" against Iran on Feb. 28.

item.title: EU leaders choose team for Ukraine peace talks after months of wavering
item.description: British representatives will be part of a team representing Europe in Ukraine peace talks.

item.title: 'We have done all our homework' to get EU candidate status: Kosovo's PM Albin Kurti
item.description: FRANCE 24 hosts Albin Kurti, the prime minister of Kosovo, a country that declared its independence from Serbia back in 2008 and sees itself as part of the European family. But four years after applying to join the EU, Kosovo has still not received candidate status. We explore Kosovo's path towards the EU, and the broader European and regional dynamics surrounding that.

item.title: Microsoft apologizes for email disruption, says AI agents not responsible
item.description: Microsoft is reporting "issues" with users accessing Outlook and Teams.

item.title: As EU grapples with fierce AI competition, summit overshadowed by elusive Ukraine-Russia peace deal
item.description: As EU leaders meet for an AI summit in Dublin, largely overshadowed by Russia's war on Ukraine, William Hilderbrandt is pleased to welcome Fabrice Pothier, CEO of Rasmussen Global. On AI, Pothier points to Europe's limited computing capacity, estimating that it barely represents "5% of what's available out there." Despite the EU's wealth of researchers and expertise, he warns that Europe is struggling to turn these resources into "real technological and industrial scale." Now, turning to the war in Ukraine, Pothier argues that European governments should focus less on "whether they have a place at the table" and more on "making Ukraine's hands stronger," particularly by providing additional air defence interceptors.

item.title: The Nvidia affair: Are markets about to fall out of love with AI?
item.description: Jensen Huang’s departure from Nvidia exposes the vulnerabilities behind the AI boom. As equities reel in response to his resignation following extramarital affairs, alleged Chinese espionage and a summons to testify before US lawmakers, questions mount over who is really in charge of tech and whether the immense capital riding on it can survive the turmoil.

item.title: The Trump administration's voter roll crusade could continue
item.description: Election officials are preparing for the Trump administration's pressure tactics over potential noncitizens on state voter rolls to continue, though recent court rulings pose new obstacles.

item.title: November 13 Paris attacks: Eleven years later, France pays tribute to victims
item.description: Eleven years on, France pays tribute to the victims of the November 13 attacks. French officials, victims’ associations and families gathered this Friday to pay their respects to those killed in the attacks in Paris on November 13, 2015.

item.title: Crossing Afghanistan along the 'highway of death'
item.description: Highway 1, or the Ring Road, connects Afghanistan's major cities. After September 11, 2001, it became a hotspot for crime and fighting, particularly between the capital Kabul and Kandahar, the Taliban's birthplace. People taking it had to navigate extortions, kidnappings and suicide bombings. What has become of the road after the US-led war and five years of Taliban rule? Our former Afghanistan correspondent Claire Billet and photojournalist Sandra Calligaro returned to the country to find out.

item.title: WATCH: 41-year-old firefighter’s life saved by heart transplant
item.description: Nico Ratto, a dad of two from New Jersey, spent 45 days hospitalized before receiving a lifesaving heart transplant.

item.title: Myanmar: Junta carries out double-tap airstrikes targeting civilians
item.description: Numerous civilian casualties have been documented in Rakhine State amid a renewed military offensive by the junta to regain control of the area. Available evidence suggests that military aircraft are deliberately targeting civilian sites and carrying out double-tap strikes.

item.title: El Niño fuels climate disasters: The high price of inaction
item.description: 2026 is set to be one of the hottest years on record, with El Niño worsening the impact of extreme weather events. With COP31 underway in Turkey, FRANCE 24 speaks with the UNDP's climate boss about the cost of waiting in a warmer world, and with one of the student activists from Pacific Island nations who took their climate fight to the UN's highest court, and won.

item.title: US military responds to 'suspected unauthorised drone activity' at UK air base
item.description: US personnel were told to take shelter at RAF Lakenheath, a major base hosting American forces in the UK, following "suspected unauthorised drone activity".

item.title: West Bank: ‘Without international trade and financial support, large settlements would not exist’
item.description: France is considering legislation to restrict trade with Israeli settlements in the occupied Palestinian territories, namely the West Bank. Ivar Ekeland, Professor Emeritus at Paris Dauphine-PSL University and Chair of the Organization of Academics for the Respect of International Law in Palestine, discusses the proposed measures with Alison Sargent. He calls for restrictions to cover n ot only goods but also services, including financial services, insurance and tourism. "Without the support of financial entities, of insurance, of providing goods and so on, settlements, big settlements, would not exist," he argues.

item.title: WATCH: Heartwarming update on Punch the Monkey
item.description: The baby macaque at Japan’s Ichikawa City Zoo became a viral sensation after turning to an IKEA toy for comfort. Nine months later, Punch has joined the troop and taken an interest in a baby macaque.

item.title: UN refugee chief Barham Salih slams 'shameful' war in Sudan, urges 'political solution'
item.description: In an interview with FRANCE 24, UN refugee chief Barham Salih called the war in Sudan "shameful" and urged the world to end it. With forced displacement at a record high, he warned that funding cuts are hurting people "in dire need". "Efficiency has its limits," he said. Salih also defended the "integrity of the asylum system".

item.title: France asks Brussels to examine Algeria's non-compliance of EU association agreement
item.description: France announced on Friday that it will ask the European Commission to "examine" Algeria's non-compliance with its EU association agreement. Earlier in July, Algiers imposed a near-blanket ban on French imports, and last month, Algeria suspended urea shipments to France.

item.title: Nvidia scandal: How close was ex-CEO to Trump?
item.description: US lawmakers have called Jensen Huang to face their questions in December after the Nvidia ex-CEO quit over extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy. The Taiwanese-born businessman was a close informal adviser to President Donald Trump on AI and had spent years lobbying against curbs on sales of advanced AI chips to China for national security reasons. Just how close Huang was to Trump and the extent of the influence tech giants have on his administration are some of the questions that still need answering, says France 24’s Douglas Herbert.

item.title: Russia strikes targets across Ukraine as Kyiv launches nearly 1,200 drones
item.description: Russian strikes hit targets across Ukraine on Thursday, with one attack damaging a hospital. Ukraine meanwhile fired almost 1,200 drones at Russian targets overnight in one of its biggest aerial attacks since Moscow’s full-scale invasion nearly five years ago.

item.title: How Sen. Chris Van Hollen plans to flex Democratic power on the foreign aid front
item.description: He's the ranking member of the Senate Foreign Relations Subcommittee that oversees health aid and he's just announced he's running for Majority Leader. He spoke to NPR about his foreign aid vision.

item.title: WATCH: Empire State Building climbers appear in court
item.description: The daredevil couple who were arrested after climbing to the top of the Empire State Building were in court on Thursday to face criminal charges and possible deportation.

item.title: Haitian forces recapture national stadium after two years of gang control
item.description: Haitian security forces regained control Thursday, November 12, of the country's main stadium that had been under gang control for two years, forcing the national football team to play elsewhere. The Haitian National Police said in a statement that it had taken "full control" of the venue with the Task Force, a private security group serving the government, after which it left the stadium under the guard of Salvadoran soldiers.

item.title: Is the worst now over for American democracy?
item.description: Over a week after the midterm elections, the dust has settled, and we can ask: is the worst now over for American democracy?

item.title: Roger Waters launches heartfelt plea for 'an end to the genocide in Gaza'
item.description: Pink Floyd co-founder Roger Waters has always mixed art with activism. A long-standing supporter of the Palestinian cause, the star guitarist has now released a re-imagined version of the rock anthem "Comfortably Numb" with Palestinian American singer Mona Miari singing in Arabic. He tells FRANCE 24's Lyana Saleh why proceeds of the record are going to the Palestine Children's Relief Fund and why he can never become "Comfortably Numb" with the violence and suffering in Gaza.

item.title: 'Devastated wasteland': Haitian security forces regain control of stadium from gangs
item.description: Haitian security forces said they have regained control of the country's main stadium, wresting it back from the gangs that have been using it for the past two years. They were assisted by the Task Force, a private security group serving the government. The stadium is now under the guard of Salvadoran soldiers. FRANCE 24's senior reporter Catherine Norris Trent, who has covered Haiti extensively, said re-taking the stadium would be a significant step in an area of the city that had been a "devastated wasteland".

item.title: The truth about Douma: How Syria covered up a chemical attack
item.description: On April 7, 2018, the Syrian town of Douma, on the outskirts of the capital Damascus, was targeted by a chemical attack. Evidence pointed to the Syrian regime, yet proof vanished, and eyewitnesses went silent. Eight years later, FRANCE 24's Jenna Le Bras tracked down survivors and witnesses of the deadly attack. She also met representatives of some of the world's most powerful institutions to understand how a massive cover-up campaign had been orchestrated by the regime, with Russian support.

item.title: Republicans dazed by midterm election defeats grapple with what went wrong
item.description: Republicans are grappling with unexpected losses after the midterm elections

item.title: Maryland Sen. Van Hollen says he will challenge Sen. Schumer for Democratic leader
item.description: Maryland Democratic Sen. Chris Van Hollen says he will challenge New York Sen. Chuck Schumer for Senate majority leader in the new Congress.

item.title: WATCH: School's ultimate class trip heads to Antarctica
item.description: ABC News' Danny New reports on a group of middle schoolers in Maryland who are about to get the snow day of their lives in the form of a class trip to Antarctica.

item.title: Jeffrey Donaldson's wife Eleanor placed on sex offenders' register after his rape conviction
item.description: Eleanor Donaldson, the wife of disgraced former DUP leader Jeffrey Donaldson, has been placed on the sex offenders' register.

item.title: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton has finalized his divorce
item.description: An attorney for Republican Ken Paxton says Texas' outgoing attorney general has finalized his divorce

item.title: WATCH: Tanker truck driver narrowly avoids train crash in Fort Worth
item.description: A tanker truck driver managed to escape from his vehicle just seconds before a train slammed into his truck.

item.title: US soldier accused of spying for Russia identified: Source
item.description: US officer who was arrested in the UK on suspicion of spying for Russia is 41-year-old Lt. Col. Brandon Tyner, according to a source familiar with the investigation.

item.title: Republicans push for Jensen Huang's testimony following Nvidia CEO's resignation
item.description: "I don't think he's got anything to hide now. Let it fly," Rep. Burchett said.

item.title: WATCH: United Airlines banning AI bots from booking flights
item.description: The airline says customers who give their personal and credit card information to AI businesses run the risk of having their sensitive data exposed.

item.title: Man shot dead in Washington DC gym is named
item.description: A man shot dead in a Washington DC gym on Thursday has been named.

item.title: WATCH: ABC's Bob Woodruff's foundation honors wounded soldiers and their families
item.description: David Muir speaks with "The Resilient" – a band made up of wounded soldiers – backstage at Bob Woodruff's annual Stand Up for Heroes, raising millions for veterans and military families.

item.title: Israeli strike on Gaza hospital kills six, health ministry says
item.description: An Israeli airstrike on a Palestinian hospital has killed at least six and wounded 28, Gaza's Health Ministry said.

item.title: WATCH: Mom becomes first woman to run 100 miles in Antarctica
item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to a Canadian ultramarathoner becoming the first woman ever to run 100 continuous miles in Antarctica.

item.title: Bomb alert at Calais train station disrupts Eurostar
item.description: A bomb alert at a French train station disrupted journeys including international travel, with Eurostar trains among those affected.

item.title: Fiery clashes erupt in Spain as millions join general strike
item.description: Unrest broke out in cities across Spain on Wednesday after millions of workers joined the country's first general strike in 14 years.

item.title: WATCH: President Trump pays tribute to veterans
item.description: President Donald Trump spoke at a Veterans Day ceremony at Arlington National Cemetery honoring fallen soldiers and addressed the war with Iran.

item.title: WATCH: Little girl rescued after sneaker wave pulls her into Pacific
item.description: The rescue was caught on camera after a child was nearly swept out to sea by a sneaker wave along the Pacific coast.

item.title: WATCH: Superhero window washers make children’s day at Omaha hospital
item.description: Patients at Children’s Nebraska were surprised by superheroes washing their windows as part of a special tradition.

item.title: WATCH: These NFL cheerleaders balance life in the military
item.description: On Veterans Day, ABC News' Danny New talks to two cheerleaders for the Philadelphia Eagles who've also served their country.
